proposals: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should publish each year, from VAHAN registration data, the number of government-owned vehicles by fuel type for the Union and each state, so the 0.6% figure from a February 2022 Lok Sabha reply is replaced by a current, official measure of government-fleet electrification.

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs should publish quarterly, city by city, the PM-eBus Sewa buses sanctioned, delivered and in service, so progress towards 10,000 buses is not frozen at the 7,293 sanctioned in a February 2025 release.

The Delhi Transport Department should publish how many of the government’s hired official vehicles had been converted to electric by the 2020 policy’s deadline and how many have been since, so the country’s sharpest fleet mandate has a published outcome, not only a commitment.

CESL should run and publish the results of an aggregated pilot tender for official passenger cars or ambulances, with discovered prices set against current procurement costs, so it is tested rather than assumed whether the 28–52% bus-price savings carry over to vehicles bought under different contracts.

The Madhya Pradesh government should report each year electric buses in its government fleet against the 40%-by-2030 target, with subsidies paid under each of the two 100-bus caps, so the EV Model Cities approach can be judged on delivered buses.
